messages:
deploy-bot: Canaries for release=chart-v2026.03 detected sidecar image drift for service=ingest-svc. expected=redwood/sidecar:v2.3.0 actual=redwood/sidecar:v2.4.0 in 3/20 canary pods. marking canary as WARN (no hard block). Logs: `kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=ingest-svc -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.containers[*].image}'`
anna_eng: ugh — that explains the increased startup errors we've been seeing in canary. Which chart values caused the bump?
matt: quick `helm get values release-ingest -n prod --revision 3` shows `sidecar.image.tag: v2.4.0` coming from our overlay. The chart version promoted was 1.9.1 (core app unchanged).
lina: is it safe to promote primary without pulling the sidecar change? can we split the canary so only traffic / subset gets the new sidecar? :thinking_face:
matt: yes — propose a two-step: 1) promote chart 1.9.1 _but_ override values to pin sidecar.tag=v2.3.0 for the main rollout; 2) keep the existing canary pool (k8s label canary=true) running with v2.4.0 for troubleshooting.
anna_eng: sketch of commands:```bash
# promote but pin sidecar
helm upgrade release-ingest charts/ingest --namespace prod --version 1.9.1 \
  --reuse-values \
  --set sidecar.image.tag=v2.3.0 \
  --set imagePromotion.metadata=manual-split-2026-03-21
# ensure canary selector unchanged
kubectl -n prod label deployment ingest-svc canary=true --overwrite
```
release-manager: timeline note — change window is open until 18:00 UTC. if we do a manual override we should call it out in release notes and on-call.
lina: what's the rollback surface if we pin and later find a config mismatch? do we risk divergence between canary and main?
matt: divergence is expected temporarily. Rollback plan: if pinned rollout shows regressions, revert to previous revision using `helm rollback release-ingest 2` and unpin values. For the canary group, we can scale down the canary label selector (`kubectl -n prod scale deployment ingest-svc --replicas=0 -l canary=true`) as an immediate mitigation.
anna_eng: I'll open a short ticket and add release-notes blurb: "Temporarily pin sidecar image to v2.3.0 during rollout; canary instances observed v2.4.0 — follow-up hotfix planned."
release-manager: ok — decision: proceed with pinned promote and maintain existing canary. @matt please execute after you confirm the helm dry-run output. post the `helm template` diff to the thread. :+1:
matt: doing dry-run now. found one additional overlay that set `sidecar.env.DEBUG=true` in the canary overlay — important: that explains higher logs. I'll include it in the ticket.
anna_eng: add to release notes: impact=low, mitigation=pin, follow-up=sidecar hotfix and synchronized chart update in next minor release.
lina: pinging infra-oncall to monitor for spike/oom for 30m after promote. @oncall-bot can you add a 30m watch? :eyes:
deploy-bot: scheduled watch job created: monitor-ingest-svc-startup (30m). alert thresholds: pod_ready_latency>20s, restart_count>3.
matt: helm template diff:```diff
--- a/templates/deployment.yaml
+++ b/templates/deployment.yaml
@@
-        image: redwood/sidecar:v2.4.0
+        image: redwood/sidecar:v2.3.0  # pinned for rollout
```
release-manager: thanks. proceed and update thread with rollout completion timestamp. keep release-notes entry brief. :rocket:
anna_eng: pushed ticket RD-5821, assigned to ops and eng-qa. I'll draft the release note and attach RD-5821.
matt: promote done at 3956781205. Helm upgrade succeeded, no immediate regressions. left canary pods with label canary=true running v2.4.0 (3 pods).
lina: monitoring green so far. will keep the 30m watch.
release-manager: closing decision thread — follow-up: schedule hotfix point release to align sidecar across overlays; assigned to @matt and @anna_eng.
